newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Pharmaceutical lists on ASX.
newsitem.headline: Australian Pharmaceutical lists on ASX.

text.p: Pharmaceutical wholesaler Australian Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd (API) closed at A$2.25 after listing on the Australian Stock Exchange on Monday, ahead of market expectations.
But the stock closed on its low for the day after opening at its high of A$2.72, and gyrating in morning trade.
Analysts said the price reflected the high level of retail support for the stock, which had been expected to list at up to A$2.00. About 516,000 shares changed hands.
API managing director Ron Rowland said he was "very pleased" with the listing price, which compared with a forecast range of A$1.60 and A$2.00.

API, a former co-operative, becomes the second listed company in the A$3.5 billion wholesale pharmaceutical market, which is contested by market leader F.H. Faulding & Co Ltd, Sigma Pharmaceuticals and API.
Rowland said API planned to boost market share to 30 percent from 26 percent within 12 months and would begin operations in South Australia in September and in Western Australia soon after.
The company is also looking to break into the A$1.5 billion hospital pharmaceutical market, currently serviced directly by manufacturers by tender with government.
"That's the trend in the United States and England," Rowland told Reuters. "Ten years ago the American wholesalers did no business with hospitals and now they have 80-90 percent of all the business."
Wholesalers mainly offered much improved levels of service, he said.
